commands.name: caveman
commands.description: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by dropping filler, articles, and pleasantries while keeping full technical accuracy. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. (user)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Drives the GUI of a visible local app window through `orca computer`: accessibility tree, clicks, typing, menus, dialogs, and screenshots in native apps and external browser windows (Chrome, Edge, Safari) or webviews. Prefer a programmatic path (shell, filesystem, git, HTTP, existing CLIs) whenever it can complete the task. Use only when a visible window needs GUI control those cannot reach. Do not use for Orca's embedded browser (`orca-cli`). (user)

commands.name: diagnose
commands.description: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. commands.name: disk-usage
commands.description: Find what is using disk space on this Mac and how to free it. Use when the disk is full or nearly full, Docker or builds fail with "no space left on device", or the user asks what is taking up storage. (user)

commands.name: edit-article
commands.description: Edit and improve articles by restructuring sections, improving clarity, and tightening prose. Use when user wants to edit, revise, or improve an article draft. (user)

commands.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
commands.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code. (user)

commands.name: grill-me

commands.name: grill-with-docs
commands.description: Grilling session that challenges your plan against the existing domain model, sharpens terminology, and updates documentation (CONTEXT.md, ADRs) inline as decisions crystallise. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan against their project's language and documented decisions. (user)

commands.name: handoff
commands.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up. (user)

commands.name: applypass-devkit:signoz-incident-evidence

commands.name: applypass-devkit:signoz-latency-spike

commands.name: applypass-devkit:signoz-log-search

commands.name: applypass-devkit:signoz-on-call-handoff

commands.name: applypass-devkit:signoz-post-deploy

Trigger after merging to main on ai_backend or apply_pass_backend, when the user says "did the deploy regress anything", "post-deploy check", "before/after metrics for the last deploy", or pastes a deploy SHA / timestamp.

commands.name: applypass-devkit:signoz-rest-api

commands.name: applypass-customer:job-search
commands.description: (applypass-customer) Search for jobs matching the user's skills, title, and location — then filter out spam and invalid listings, classify metadata, and return a curated set ready for resume matching. commands.name: applypass-customer:profile-setup
commands.description: (applypass-customer) Help a registered ApplyPass user review their profile, check pre-computed job matches, and get application answers written for specific listings. Use this skill whenever the user mentions their ApplyPass account, wants to see their matches, asks how many jobs they've applied to, wants to write an application essay, or says something like "show me my jobs" or "write me an answer for this question." Also trigger when someone with an account wants to compare specific jobs or track their application progress.

commands.name: applypass-customer:resume-match
commands.description: (applypass-customer) Match a resume against job listings and return ranked scores. Use this skill whenever the user wants to find jobs that fit their resume, score a set of jobs against a candidate, compare job listings side-by-side for fit, or asks about best-fit roles — even if they don't say "resume match" explicitly. Works with a PDF upload, pasted resume text, or a stored ApplyPass account. Also use when the user has already run /job-search and wants to rank those results against their resume.

commands.name: applypass-support:application-quality-diagnosis
commands.description: (applypass-support) Diagnose why an ApplyPass customer's auto-generated applications, cover letters, or answers are wrong — hallucinated content, wrong company name, generic boilerplate, wrong tone, an answer that contradicts the customer's profile (e.g. visa sponsorship for a US citizen, a past start date). Walks the answer-generation pipeline and identifies the most likely cause. Trigger when /triage-customer-complaint classifies a complaint as bad-applications, or the user says "answers are hallucinated", "wrong company in cover letter", "answered with a past date", "says I need visa sponsorship but I'm a citizen", "application content is generic".

commands.name: applypass-support:application-volume-diagnosis
commands.description: (applypass-support) Diagnose why an ApplyPass customer is not getting enough applications submitted — "no apps for a week", "4300 matches but nothing applied", "applier is on but quiet", a drop in volume after a profile change. Runs the match -> queue -> apply funnel for the jsp_id and separates a supply problem (excluded job sources) from a real bug. This is a VOLUME question, distinct from /match-quality-diagnosis (relevance) and /applier-failure-diagnosis (one match that errored). Trigger when /triage-customer-complaint classifies a complaint as low volume, or the user says "not enough applications", "applications stopped", "matches aren't turning into applications", "queue isn't moving", "why so few applies".

commands.name: applypass-support:applier-failure-diagnosis
commands.description: (applypass-support) Diagnose why an ApplyPass auto-application failed to submit through an ATS — OTP/IMAP credential failures, "started but not submitted", Ashby spam-flagging, captcha, ATS API changes, or companies that require email verification before submission. Walks the applier pipeline for a specific match, identifies the ATS-specific failure mode, and proposes a fix. Trigger when /triage-customer-complaint classifies a complaint as an applier failure, when /match-trace finds application_submission_error set, or when the user says "applications not going out", "applier not sending", "started not submitted", "OTP failed", "invalid credentials", "captcha failed", "no applications showing in my Workday/Greenhouse account".

commands.name: applypass-support:classifier-accuracy-check
commands.description: (applypass-support) Diagnose ApplyPass job classifier accuracy issues — wrong employment type (contract vs FT), wrong remote/onsite flag, wrong seniority, wrong salary band, wrong role/domain. Re-classifies the disputed listing from its raw ATS payload, compares against the cached classification, and identifies whether the issue is a classifier bug, a stale cache, or an ATS data gap. Trigger when /triage-customer-complaint classifies a complaint as classifier-accuracy, or the user says "this job is mislabeled", "classifier got it wrong", "labeled remote but isn't", "labeled FT but it's contract", "wrong salary band", "wrong domain".

commands.name: applypass-support:customer-lookup
commands.description: (applypass-support) Look up an ApplyPass customer by email (or name) to find their jsp_id, client_id, subscription tier, JSP profile, and resume. Returns a structured profile used as the input to /match-trace and all downstream diagnosis skills. Trigger when the user says "look up <email>", "find this customer", "who is <email>", "what's their jsp_id", "pull <customer>'s account", or any time another applypass-support skill needs the customer's identifiers before running diagnostics.

commands.name: applypass-support:escalation-detector
commands.description: (applypass-support) Proactively detect ApplyPass escalations before customer-success reports them. Run on a schedule (every ~15 min), it checks early-signal metrics in SigNoz and Metabase for the high-frequency escalation families — resume-pipeline failures, IMAP/credential errors, OTP timeouts, captcha solve-rate drops, applier-volume drops, runaway jobs — and posts a batched alert to #engineering with a pre-staged triage hand-off when a signal trips. Trigger when the user says "set up proactive detection", "alert me before CS does", "build escalation monitoring", "run the escalation detector", or when invoked by a scheduled task.

commands.name: applypass-support:escalation-postmortem-capture
commands.description: (applypass-support) After an ApplyPass escalation is resolved, capture the diagnostic path as a structured postmortem so the next similar escalation is triaged in seconds. Records the symptom phrasing, the identifier path, the root-cause family, the fix, and the prevention; saves it to the PKM vault; and — when the issue is novel — proposes a new row for escalation-playbook.md. This is the write side of the known-issue catalog that /triage-customer-complaint reads. Trigger when the user says "capture this escalation", "save this triage", "log this postmortem", "this is resolved — record it", or at the end of any applypass-support diagnosis once a fix is confirmed.

commands.name: applypass-support:match-quality-diagnosis
commands.description: (applypass-support) Diagnose why an ApplyPass customer is getting bad job matches — irrelevant roles, wrong location, wrong seniority, wrong industry, matches that don't fit the resume. Walks the matching pipeline (resume embedding -> cosine similarity -> CosineProjectionModel -> XGBoost re-ranker -> JSP filters) using the applypass MCP, identifies the most likely root cause, and proposes a fix. This is a RELEVANCE skill — for "not enough applications" use /application-volume-diagnosis instead. Trigger when the user says "matches are bad", "wrong jobs being shown", "irrelevant matches", "diagnose match quality for <jsp>", or when /triage-customer-complaint classifies a complaint as bad-matches.

commands.name: applypass-support:match-trace
commands.description: (applypass-support) Trace an ApplyPass customer issue from their jsp_id down to the specific job_id and match_id that failed, and pull that match's full pipeline state (match score, queue status, application_submitted, in_processing_status, submission error, retry count, ATS). This is the bridge between /customer-lookup (who) and the stage-4 diagnosis skills (why). Trigger when you have a jsp_id and need to find "which match was the issue", when a complaint names a specific job or company, when the user says "trace this match", "find the match_id", "what happened to this application", "which job failed for <customer>", or whenever a diagnosis skill needs a match_id and per-match state.

commands.name: applypass-support:resume-pipeline-diagnose
commands.description: (applypass-support) Diagnose ApplyPass resume-pipeline failures — a finalized resume that never uploaded, too many pages, wrong file extension, file too big, an S3/Spaces fetch timeout, or `Failed to get resume file for jsp` appearing in autoapplier logs. Walks the upload -> finalize -> object-storage -> fetch pipeline, identifies the failed stage, and produces a paste-ready CS message for the user-side fix. This covers resume *delivery* failures (the file the applier can't get) — for resume *content* parsing into bad matches use /match-quality-diagnosis. Trigger when /triage-customer-complaint classifies a complaint as resume-pipeline, or the user says "resume issue", "finalized resume missing", "Failed to get resume file", "my apps are failing because of my resume", "resume won't upload", "downloadlatestResumeFinalizedFile errors".

commands.name: applypass-support:triage-customer-complaint
commands.description: (applypass-support) Entry point for ApplyPass customer complaint triage. Use whenever a customer complaint comes in via Slack or Gmail and the engineer needs to diagnose root cause. Parses the complaint, classifies it (bad matches / low volume / applier failure / bad applications / classifier issue / data integrity / infra), looks up the customer, traces it to the failing match, hands off to the right diagnosis skill, and posts a resolution. Trigger on phrases like "customer complaint", "user says their matches are wrong", "CS forwarded this customer issue", "triage this support ticket", "<customer email> is complaining about <X>", "applications not going out for <user>", or when a Slack/Gmail thread is provided with a customer issue.

commands.description: (applypass-coach) Review, edit, and rewrite resume bullets into a prioritized, evidence-cited edit list with Google XYZ rewrites. commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx).
